$comment: Tool definitions for the plant agent (Anthropic tool-use / MCP input_schema format). The agent never computes losses itself: it calls these and quotes only text from the returned `facts`, citing their ids.

scope.description: Which machines and days to analyse. Omit for the whole plant. Days are plant day indices; tools that compare a recent window against a baseline choose their own windows and only use day_to.

tools.name: cluster_stops
tools.description: Groups stop events into families (k-means) and separates recurring patterns from irregular stops (DBSCAN). Returns, per family: stops, hours stopped, median duration, typical time of day, share without a reason, a suggested reason with confidence, and the machines with most time. Also lists the longest irregular stops. Use for: 'where did the time go', 'which stops have no reason', 'what were the unusual stops'.

min_confidence.description: Minimum share of justified stops agreeing on a reason before a family gets a suggestion.

tools.name: detect_cycle_drift
tools.description: Finds machines whose recent part cycles left their normal envelope (nearest-neighbour distance in a 6-signal space, per machine and program, last 7 days vs the 21 days before). Returns flagged machines with cycle-time change in %, share of cycles outside the envelope, estimated start date and the signals that moved most. New programs without a baseline are listed, not scored. Use for: 'is anything getting slower', 'why is output down on machine X'.

tools.name: rank_loss_drivers
tools.description: Ranks the conditions most associated with unplanned stop minutes per available machine-hour (random forest + permutation importance on held-out hours): supplier batch, shift, tool age, days since maintenance, operator, etc. Uses whichever of those columns the hours table has. Absent columns are listed in result.missing_features and are not imputed. Returns the ranking, effect sizes for the top drivers, model fit (holdout R²) and confounding caveats. Results are associations, not causes. Use for: 'what drives our losses', 'is supplier X worse'.

tools.name: signal_health
tools.description: Checks whether each machine's 12 signals (loads, speeds, currents, vibration, temperatures, coolant) still move together the way they did in the reference window (PCA, SPE and Hotelling T² per machine and program). Returns abnormal machines, the share of abnormal cycles, the start date and the signals that deviate most. Catches faults that do not change cycle time (e.g. a weakening coolant pump). Use for: 'anything wrong with the machines', maintenance questions.

envelope.$comment: Every tool returns this shape. Only `facts[].text` may be quoted; cite as [<facts[].id>]. If parity.citable is false, re-run on the stock backend or answer without the number.

call_id.description: Deterministic id: same tool, params, data and backend give the same id.
